facts.statement: The genus Irritator was described by Martill et al. in 1996.
facts.quote: authority: Martill et al., 1996

facts.statement: The holotype skull was acquired by fossil dealers and sold to the State Museum of Natural History Stuttgart.
facts.quote: Fossil dealers had acquired this skull and sold it to the State Museum of Natural History Stuttgart.

facts.statement: The genus name Irritator refers to the irritation paleontologists felt because the skull was heavily damaged and altered by collectors.
facts.quote: The genus name comes from the word "irritation", reflecting the feelings of paleontologists who found the skull had been heavily damaged and altered by the collectors.

facts.statement: The species name challengeri honors the fictional character Professor Challenger from Arthur Conan Doyle's novels.
facts.quote: The species name is a homage to the fictional character Professor Challenger from Arthur Conan Doyle's novels.

facts.statement: Irritator was estimated to be between 6 and 8 meters long and weigh around 1 ton, making it one of the smallest known spinosaurids.
facts.quote: Estimated at between 6 and 8 m in length, Irritator weighed around 1 t, making it one of the smallest spinosaurids known.

facts.statement: Irritator had a long, shallow, and slender snout lined with straight, unserrated conical teeth.
facts.quote: Its long, shallow and slender snout was lined with straight and unserrated conical teeth.

facts.statement: A thin sagittal crest ran along the top of Irritator's head, likely anchoring powerful neck muscles.
facts.quote: Lengthwise atop the head ran a thin sagittal crest, to which powerful neck muscles were likely anchored.

facts.statement: Irritator's nostrils were positioned far back on the snout, and a rigid secondary palate likely strengthened its jaw during feeding.
facts.quote: The nostrils were positioned far back from the tip of the snout, and a rigid secondary palate on the roof of the mouth would have strengthened the jaw when feeding.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Irritator challengeri is a subadult and represents the most completely preserved spinosaurid skull ever found.
facts.quote: Belonging to a subadult, Irritator challengeris holotype remains the most completely preserved spinosaurid skull yet found.

facts.statement: Irritator was identified as a spinosaurid theropod in 1996.
facts.quote: In 1996, the animal was identified as a spinosaurid theropod.

facts.statement: The holotype skull was redescribed in 2002, confirming its classification as a spinosaurid.
facts.quote: The holotype skull was thoroughly prepared before being redescribed in 2002, confirming this classification.

facts.statement: Both Irritator and Angaturama belong to the Spinosaurinae subfamily.
facts.quote: Both Irritator and Angaturama belong to the Spinosaurinae subfamily.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Irritator had a generalist diet similar to modern crocodilians, likely preying mainly on fish and other small animals.
facts.quote: A generalist diet—like that of today's crocodilians—has been suggested; Irritator might have preyed mainly on fish and any other small prey animals it could catch.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence indicates an individual Irritator ate a pterosaur, either by hunting or scavenging.
facts.quote: Fossil evidence is known of an individual that ate a pterosaur, either from hunting or scavenging it.

facts.statement: Irritator may have had semiaquatic habits and lived in a tropical coastal lagoon environment surrounded by dry regions.
facts.quote: Irritator may have had semiaquatic habits, and inhabited the tropical environment of a coastal lagoon surrounded by dry regions.

facts.statement: Some paleontologists consider Angaturama limai a potential junior synonym of Irritator.
facts.quote: Some paleontologists regard Angaturama limai—known from a snout tip that was described a few weeks later also in 1996—as a potential junior synonym of Irritator.

facts.statement: The holotype skull of Irritator was found near Santana do Cariri in northeastern Brazil.
facts.quote: The holotype of Irritator was excavated from a chalk concretion containing the rear of a large skull with lower jaws near the town of Santana do Cariri in northeastern Brazil.

facts.statement: The fossil was acquired by traffickers and taken to the State Museum of Natural History in Stuttgart, Germany.
facts.quote: This fossil was acquired by fossil traffickers and taken to the State Museum of Natural History in Stuttgart, Germany.

facts.statement: Irritator challengeri was first scientifically described in February 1996 by David M. Martill, Arthur R.I. Cruickshank, Eberhard Frey, Philip G. Small, and Maria Clarke.
facts.quote: The skull (designated SMNS 58022) became the holotype specimen of the new genus and species Irritator challengeri in February 1996, when it was first scientifically described by paleontologists David M. Martill, Arthur R.I. Cruickshank, Eberhard Frey, Philip G. Small and Maria Clarke.

facts.statement: Fossil traders obscured the skull with plaster to make it appear more complete, a common practice among local collectors.
facts.quote: In hopes of making it look more complete and valuable, the fossil traders had severely obscured the skull beneath plaster; a widespread practice among local collectors in the Chapada do Araripe, especially on fish fossils.

facts.statement: The skull is designated specimen number SMNS 58022.
facts.quote: The skull (designated SMNS 58022) became the holotype specimen of the new genus and species Irritator challengeri in February 1996, when it was first scientifically described by paleontologists David M. Martill, Arthur R.I. Cruickshank, Eberhard Frey, Philip G. Small and Maria Clarke.

facts.statement: The specific name challengeri honors Professor Challenger, a character from Arthur Conan Doyle's novel The Lost World.
facts.quote: The type species, Irritator challengeri, was named after Professor Challenger, a character in Arthur Conan Doyle's novels, specifically The Lost World.

facts.statement: A detailed redescription of the specimen was published in 2002 after the skull bones were fully extracted by Diane M. Scott under the supervision of Hans-Dieter Sues.
facts.quote: Under the supervision of American paleontologist Hans-Dieter Sues, technician Diane M. Scott from the University of Toronto Mississauga assumed the task of fully extracting the skull bones from the rock, allowing for a detailed redescription in 2002.

facts.statement: Researchers initially suggested Irritator might be a junior synonym of Spinosaurus due to shared dental features.
facts.quote: As in the previous study, Sues and colleagues regarded the African and possibly South American genus Spinosaurus as the most similar taxon to Irritator, because they shared many dental features, including mostly straight conical tooth crowns, thin enamel, well-defined edges with no serrations, and lengthwise fluting.

facts.statement: The specimen most probably originates from the Romualdo Formation, though the exact site is uncertain due to trafficking.
facts.quote: Although the site of discovery is uncertain due to it having been trafficked out of Brazil and the lack of provenance documentation presented in the species description, the specimen most probably stems from the Romualdo Formation (previously designated the Romualdo Member of the then Santana Formation).

facts.statement: Local dealers suggested the fossil came from near the village of Buxexé at a height of approximately 650 meters.
facts.quote: Questioning of local fossil dealers hinted at a locality near the village of Buxexé close to Santana Do Cariri at the flank of the Chapada do Araripe, at a height of approximately 650 m.

facts.statement: Irritator was the first dinosaur described from the Romualdo Formation and its holotype is the most completely preserved spinosaurid skull known.
facts.quote: Irritator challengeri was the first dinosaur described from the Romualdo Formation, and its holotype specimen represents the most completely preserved spinosaurid skull known.

facts.statement: Angaturama limai was described in February 1996 by Alexander W. A. Kellner and Diogenes de Almeida Campos.
facts.quote: Angaturama limai, another spinosaurid from the same time and place as Irritator challengeri, was described by the Brazilian paleontologists Alexander W. A. Kellner and Diogenes de Almeida Campos in February 1996.

facts.statement: Multiple authors from 2002 to 2015 supported the conclusion that Angaturama is a synonym of Irritator.
facts.quote: Authors including Éric Buffetaut and Mohamed Ouaja in 2002, Cristiano Dal Sasso and colleagues in 2005, Tor G. Bertin in 2010, Darren Naish in 2013, and Madani Benyoucef and colleagues in 2015 supported this conclusion.

facts.statement: Kellner and Campos, and later Machado and Kellner, argued that the fossils belong to two different genera because the Angaturama holotype is more laterally flattened.
facts.quote: Some objection has been raised to these assertions. Kellner and Campos in 2000 and Brazilian paleontologist Elaine B. Machado and Kellner in 2005 expressed the opinion that the fossils come from two different genera, and that the holotype of Angaturama limai was clearly more laterally flattened than that of Irritator challengeri.

facts.statement: If the two genera are the same, Irritator is the valid name because it was published almost a month before Angaturama.
facts.quote: If Angaturama and Irritator are regarded as a member of the same genus, the latter would be the valid scientific name under rules of priority, since it was named almost a month earlier.

facts.statement: In 2023, Schade and colleagues could not confirm tooth position overlap or resolve the synonymy issue due to differing interpretations.
facts.quote: In 2023, German paleontologist Marco Schade and colleagues could not confirm the overlap in tooth positions due to interpreting them differently, and could not provide information to resolve the issue.

facts.statement: In 2004, paleontologists unearthed a spinal column fragment (MN 4743-V) from the Romualdo Formation.
facts.quote: In 2004, parts of a spinal column (MN 4743-V) were unearthed at the formation.

facts.statement: In 2007, Machado and Kellner tentatively assigned a rib fragment (MN 7021-V) to the Spinosauridae.
facts.quote: In 2007, Machado and Kellner tentatively referred a rib fragment (MN 7021-V) to the Spinosauridae.

facts.statement: The most complete spinosaur specimen from the Romualdo Formation is the partial skeleton MN 4819-V, which lacks a skull.
facts.quote: The most complete spinosaur specimen retrieved from the Romualdo Formation is MN 4819-V, a partial skeleton lacking the skull.

facts.statement: In 2018, Tito Aureliano and colleagues described LPP-PV-0042, a left tibia fragment from a large individual.
facts.quote: In 2018, Tito Aureliano and his team described LPP-PV-0042, part of a left tibia from a particularly large individual.

facts.statement: Most spinosaurid fossils from the Romualdo Formation were collected under uncontrolled conditions for the illegal fossil trade.
facts.quote: As is common with fossils from the Araripe Basin, the majority of spinosaurid material from the Romualdo Formation was collected under uncontrolled circumstances for use in the illegal fossil trade.

facts.statement: The Angaturama replica was the centerpiece of the 'Dinossauros no Sertão' exhibit, which opened in March 2009 as the first large carnivorous Brazilian dinosaur on display.
facts.quote: It was the centerpiece of the Dinossauros no Sertão (Dinosaurs of Sertão) exhibit, which opened to the public in March 2009, becoming the first large carnivorous Brazilian dinosaur to be put on display.

facts.statement: In 2011, the spinosaur Oxalaia quilombensis was named and described from the Alcântara Formation in the São Luís Basin.
facts.quote: In 2011, a third Brazilian spinosaur, Oxalaia quilombensis, was named and described from the Alcântara Formation of the Itapecuru Group, part of the São Luís Basin.

facts.statement: Irritator was smaller than other known spinosaurids even according to maximum size estimates.
facts.quote: Even by maximal size estimates, Irritator was smaller than other known spinosaurids.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated Irritator's length at 7.5 meters and weight at 1 ton.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul calculated its length at 7.5 m and weight at 1 t.

facts.statement: Thomas R. Holtz Jr. estimated Irritator's length at 8 meters and weight between 0.9 and 3.6 tons.
facts.quote: Thomas R. Holtz Jr. published a higher estimate of 8 m, with a weight between 0.9 to 3.6 t.

facts.statement: Dougal Dixon estimated Irritator to be 6 meters long and 2 meters high.
facts.quote: Estimates by Dougal Dixon were lower at 6 m long and 2 m high.

facts.statement: Scaling studies by Aureliano and colleagues suggested the Irritator holotype was 6.5 meters long, while the Angaturama holotype was 8.3 meters long.
facts.quote: When scaled by Aureliano and colleagues, the reconstructions from the study by Sales and Schultz provided a length of 6.5 m for the Irritator challengeri holotype, and 8.3 m for the Angaturama limai holotype.

facts.statement: Unfused skull bones in the Irritator holotype indicate the specimen was a subadult.
facts.quote: Some of the skull bones of the former holotype had not yet fully co-ossified (fused), indicating that the specimen belonged to a subadult.

facts.statement: Based on a tibia fragment (LPP-PV-0042), Aureliano and colleagues estimated the individual's length at roughly 10 meters.
facts.quote: Although LPP-PV-0042 is represented only by a tibia fragment, Aureliano and colleagues estimated its length at roughly 10 m.

facts.statement: The skull of Irritator was long, narrow, and somewhat triangular in cross-section.
facts.quote: Irritators skull was long, narrow, and somewhat triangular in cross section.

facts.statement: Unlike Baryonyx, the lacrimal bone of Irritator did not form a bony horn core.
facts.quote: Unlike in Baryonyx, Irritators lacrimal did not form a bony horn core.

facts.statement: Irritator possessed straight or faintly recurved conical teeth with sharply defined but unserrated edges.
facts.quote: Irritator had straight or only faintly recurved conical teeth, bearing sharply defined but unserrated edges.

facts.statement: Nine teeth are preserved in each maxilla of the Irritator holotype, with traces of a tenth tooth found in the rock matrix.
facts.quote: Both of Irritators maxillae preserve nine teeth, although the left maxilla's tooth crowns are more intact, and there are traces of a tenth tooth in the rock matrix.

facts.statement: The front of the Angaturama limai snout was expanded to form a spoon-shaped terminal rosette characteristic of spinosaurids.
facts.quote: The front of the snout was expanded, forming the spoon-shaped terminal rosette characteristic of spinosaurids.

facts.statement: The premaxillae of Angaturama limai connected at the bottom to form a secondary palate, partially contributed to by processes from the maxillae.
facts.quote: The premaxillae connected with each other on the bottom to form Angaturamas secondary palate, which was also partially contributed to by two processes extending from the maxillae.

facts.statement: Angaturama limai possessed strongly extended, straight teeth with unserrated conical crowns measuring 6 to 40 mm in length.
facts.quote: The strongly extended and straight teeth with unserrated conical crowns, which measured 6 to 40 mm in length, were singly embedded.

facts.statement: The elongated neural spines of the sacrum in Irritator would have been covered in skin to form a sail down the animal's back.
facts.quote: In life, these would have been covered in skin, forming a "sail" down the animal's back.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated the maximum length of Irritator at 7.5 meters and its weight at 1 tonne.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul calculó su longitud en 7,5 metros y su peso en 1 tonelada.

facts.statement: Thomas R. Holtz Jr. estimated the length of Irritator at 8 meters with a weight between 0.9 and 3.6 tonnes.
facts.quote: Thomas R. Holtz Jr. publicó una estimación más alta de 8 metros, con un peso entre 0,9 y 3,6 toneladas.

facts.statement: Dougal Dixon estimated the length of Irritator to be less than 6 meters and the height at 2 meters.
facts.quote: Dougal Dixon fueron menores a 6 metros de largo y 2 de alto.

facts.statement: Reconstructions by Sales and Schultz provided a length of 6.5 meters for the holotype Irritator challengeri and 8.3 meters for Angaturama limai.
facts.quote: las reconstrucciones del estudio de Sales y Schultz proporcionaron una longitud de 6,5 metros ara el holotipo Irritator challengeri y 8,3 metros para el de Angaturama limai.

facts.statement: Some skull bones of the holotype were not fully ossified, indicating the specimen belonged to a subadult.
facts.quote: Algunos de los huesos del cráneo del holotipo aún no se habían osificado completamente, es decir fusionados, lo que indica que el espécimen pertenecía a un subadulto.

facts.statement: The partial spinosaurid skeleton MN 4819-V represented an individual of moderate size, estimated by Machado at 5 to 6 meters in length.
facts.quote: El esqueleto de espinosaurino parcial MN 4819-V representó a un individuo de tamaño moderado, estimado por Machado en 5 a 6 metros de longitud.

facts.statement: Although LPP-PV-0042 is represented only by a tibia fragment, Aureliano and colleagues estimated its length at approximately 10 meters.
facts.quote: Aunque LPP-PV-0042 está representado solo por un fragmento de tibia, Aureliano y sus colegas estimaron su longitud en aproximadamente 10 metros.

facts.statement: The preserved skull of Irritator is 16.5 cm high, 10 cm wide, with a total estimated length of approximately 60 cm.
facts.quote: El cráneo conservado tiene 16,5 centímetros De altura y 10 de ancho, su longitud total se ha estimado en aproximadamente 60 centímetros

facts.statement: Like all spinosaurids, the maxillae of Irritator extended below and beyond the nasal openings to form a long, low branch creating the lower border of the opening.
facts.quote: Como en todos los espinosáuridos, los maxilares, los huesos principales de la mandíbula superior, se extendían por debajo y más allá de las fosas nasales en una rama larga y baja que formaba el borde inferior de esta abertura

facts.statement: The nasal openings of Irritator were proportionally and absolutely smaller than in Suchomimus and Baryonyx, but larger than in Spinosaurus.
facts.quote: Las fosas nasales de Irritator fueron proporcionalmente y absolutamente más pequeñas que en Suchomimus y Baryonyx, pero más grandes que las de Spinosaurus.

facts.statement: The lacrimal bone separated the orbit from the antorbital fenestra in Irritator, forming posterior margins with an angle of 40 degrees, similar to Baryonyx where the angle is 35 degrees.
facts.quote: El hueso lagrimal separó la órbita de la fenestra antorbital, formando los márgenes traseros superior e inferior de esta última con dos procesos que incluían un ángulo de 40 grados, similar a Baryonyx, donde es de 35 grados.

facts.statement: A thin sagittal crest built from elongated nasal bones rose along the midline of the skull and stopped just above the eye in a slightly flattened bump.
facts.quote: miniaturadeimagen|derecha|Cráneo. Una cresta sagital delgada, construida a partir de los huesos nasales alargados, subía por la línea media del cráneo antes de detenerse justo encima del ojo en un bulto ligeramente aplanado.

facts.statement: Like other members of its family, Irritator possessed a long bony structure in the palate called a secondary palate that separated the mouth from the nasal cavity.
facts.quote: Como otros en su familia , Irritador poseía una estructura larga y ósea en el paladar, llamada paladar secundario, que separa la boca de la cavidad nasal.

facts.statement: The holotype Irritator challengeri is unique as one of the few non-avian dinosaur fossils found with a preserved stirrup bone.
facts.quote: El holotipo Irritator challengeri es único, ya que es uno de los poco fósiles de dinosaurios no aviares que se encuentran con un estribo conservado.

facts.statement: The species Irritator challengeri was described by Martill et al. in 1996.
facts.quote: species_authority: Martill et al, 1996

facts.statement: Irritator lived during the middle Cretaceous, approximately 110 million years ago in the Albian stage, in what is now South America.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 110 millones de años, en el Albiense, en lo que hoy es Sudamérica.

facts.statement: Irritator was found in the Santana Formation in Brazil.
facts.quote: Encontrado en la Formación Santana, en Brasil

facts.statement: Many researchers consider the genus Irritator to be a synonym of Angaturama limai, which lived in the same location and site.
facts.quote: Este género es considerado por muchos como un sinónimo de Angaturama limai, que viviera en el mismo lugar y sitio que el Irritator.

facts.statement: The remains of Angaturama limai appear to complete the skull of Irritator, suggesting they might belong to the same specimen.
facts.quote: Los restos de este curiosamente parecen terminar el cráneo de Irritator, significando que podrían pertenecer al mismo espécimen.

facts.statement: Irritator possessed conical, straight or only slightly recurved teeth with well-defined edges but without serrations.
facts.quote: El Irritador tenía dientes cónicos rectos o solo ligeramente recurvados, con bordes bien definidos pero sin serrar.

facts.statement: Longitudinal crests were present on the tooth crowns of Irritator, a dental trait common among spinosaurids.
facts.quote: Crestas longitudinales estaban presentes en sus coronas dentales, un rasgo dental común entre los espinosáuridos.

facts.statement: Both sides of Irritator's teeth were striated, similar to Spinosaurus, whereas Baryonyx exhibited striations only on the lingual side facing inward.
facts.quote: Ambos lados de los dientes de Irritator fueron estriados, como en Spinosaurus, mientras que Baryonyx los exhibía solo en el lado lingual, mirando hacia adentro.

facts.statement: Irritator's teeth had a circular cross-section, contrasting with the laterally flattened condition of most theropod teeth.
facts.quote: Los dientes del Irritador tenían una sección transversal circular, en oposición a la condición aplanada lateralmente de la mayoría de los dientes de terópodos.

facts.statement: The enamel layer of Irritator's teeth was thin and had a finely wrinkled texture, also observed in Baryonyx.
facts.quote: El esmalte, primera capa de los dientes, era delgada, con una textura finamente arrugada también observada en Baryonyx.

facts.statement: Both upper jaws of Irritator preserve nine teeth, though the left maxilla crowns are more intact, with traces of a tenth tooth found in the rock matrix.
facts.quote: Ambos maxilares de Irritator preservan nueve dientes, aunque coronas de los dientes del maxilar superior izquierda están más intactos, y hay rastros de un décimo diente en la matriz de la roca.

facts.statement: The first and second preserved maxillary teeth were the largest, measuring 32 millimeters and 40 millimeters in crown length respectively.
facts.quote: El primer y segundo dientes maxilares preservados fueron los más grandes, con 32 milímetros y 40 milímetros en la longitud de la corona.

facts.statement: The remaining seven teeth became progressively smaller towards the rear, with one of the last measuring approximately 6 millimeters.
facts.quote: Los siete dientes restantes se hicieron progresivamente más pequeños hacia la parte posterior, uno de los últimos medía 6 milímetros aproximadamente.

facts.statement: Computed tomography scans of the specimen revealed replacement teeth on both sides of the upper jaw.
facts.quote: Las tomografías computarizadas realizadas en la muestra revelaron dientes de reemplazo en ambos lados de la mandíbula superior.

facts.statement: The tooth roots of Irritator extended deeply into the maxilla and converged near the midline, almost reaching the top of the skull.
facts.quote: Sus raíces se adentraron profundamente en el maxilar y convergieron cerca de la línea media, casi llegando a la parte superior del cráneo.

facts.statement: Comparisons with Irritator's relatives suggest the maxillae were likely lined with a total of 11 teeth each, similar to the 12 teeth found in the MSNM V4047 fossil referred to Spinosaurus.
facts.quote: Según las comparaciones con los familiares de Irritator, los maxilares probablemente estaban forrados con un total de 11 dientes cada uno, similar al número de 12 dientes en el MSNM V4047, un fósil de la mandíbula superior referido a Spinosaurus.

facts.statement: The last tooth of Irritator's left maxilla had not yet erupted completely, with only the tip visible.
facts.quote: El último diente del maxilar izquierdo de Irritator no había erupcionado todavía completamente, y sólo la punta de la misma era visible.

facts.statement: Irritator belongs to the parent group Spinosaurinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Spinosaurinae

facts.statement: Irritator is classified in the family Spinosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Spinosauridae

facts.statement: Irritator lived during the Aptian stage, between 119.57 and 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (119.57 to 113.2 million years ago)
